findings.problem: The regex assertion `not.toMatch(/^[^,]*GeistMono/)` is vacuously passing in all four test suites. The regex anchors at the start of the string and matches only non-comma characters before requiring 'GeistMono', but GeistMono always appears after the first comma in a var() declaration (e.g. `font-family: var(--font-family-body, GeistMono, monospace)`), so the regex never matches it. Additionally, `toContain('Geist')` also passes for 'GeistMono' since it is a substring. Neither assertion can catch a wrong fallback.
findings.impact: A developer could write `var(--font-family-body, GeistMono, monospace)` in any of the four SCSS files and all test suites would still pass green, defeating the purpose of the fallback-font guard.
findings.recommendation: Replace `expect(d).not.toMatch(/^[^,]*GeistMono/)` with `expect(d).not.toContain('GeistMono')` in all four test files (Markdown.font.integration.test.tsx, ThinkingLoader.test.tsx, ThoughtDocument.font.test.tsx, ChatAiMessage.font.test.tsx).

findings.problem: The font test suites for ChatAiMessage, ThinkingLoader, and ThoughtDocument only verify that the SCSS file contains the expected CSS variable declaration. No test renders the component and asserts that the new CSS class name (`ai-message-edit-textarea`, `thinking-loader`, `thought-document`, `thought-document-toggle`) is actually present on the correct DOM element. Removing a class name from cn() in any TSX file would leave all tests green.
findings.impact: The TSX wiring (class applied to element) is unverified. A future refactor that drops a class from cn() silently breaks the font fix without any test failing.
findings.recommendation: For each affected component, add a render-level assertion: render the component, find the target element, and assert `classList.contains('<class-name>')` is true. For ChatAiMessage, render with isEditing state active to expose the textarea.
